New: better dictation for mixed-language speech, and automatic pull request reviews.

What's new

- Dictation picks up names and jargon better. A built-in list of developer terms, your own "My words" list, the app you are in and, in a terminal or editor, the repo and branch of your latest Claude session are given to the speech engine and to the clean-up.
- New "Recogniser" setting: Automatic, Apple Dictation or Apple Speech. Automatic picks the engine that did best in our tests for the language you chose. New setups start with Hindi (India), which handles Hindi–English mixed speech in Latin script better than English (India).
- Claude clean-up now uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 (your own API key, as before).
- Automatic PR reviews (Bitbucket): when you are a reviewer on an open pull request in one of the repos you pick in Setup, AI Notch runs your Claude Code review skill on it in the background, once per new commit, using your own Claude Code sign-in. The PR row shows the progress and the verdict, and View report opens the findings and drafted comments. Nothing is posted to the pull request on its own.
- Reviews show under Agents as `PR review #<n> · <repo>`, with their subagents nested.
- Approve and Request changes from the PR row: each takes a click and a confirm. Approve is offered only when the verdict is APPROVE with no blocking findings, the pipeline is green and nothing was pushed since the review. Needs a separate Bitbucket API token with write access to pull requests, kept in the Keychain.
- Reviews are read-only: they load none of your Claude Code settings, may only run read-only git and search commands, and can write only to their own folder.

Limits

- A review uses your Claude Code plan like any other session; a large pull request can take several minutes.
- One review runs at a time. A review cut off by quitting the app is started again once on the next launch.
- The review skill and its agents are yours: set their names in Setup → Pull requests (default `pr-review`). Auto-review runs only for the repos listed under Auto-review repos, which is empty until you add some.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, the app is signed ad hoc, so macOS forgets Microphone, Input Monitoring and Accessibility: remove AI Notch from each list in System Settings → Privacy & Security, add it again, then quit and reopen the app.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later (dictation: macOS 26).
